campaign_id: qwen35-4b-w4a16 depth sweep e4/e5/e6 vs published v1 (2026-09-08, one B70)
question: The 4B inherited MTP depth 3 from the FP8 sweep exactly as the 9B did. On the 9B every depth from 3 to 6 was lossless while FP8 held only at 3, because depth changes the verify step's row count and this kernel is row-count invariant. This asks the same of the 4B, and whether a smaller target makes deeper drafts pay.
finding: Every depth from 3 to 6 is lossless on the 4B as well: G1, G2 and both G3 comparisons matched 12/12 at all four depths. That is the same result as the 9B, on a second model, and it is a fifth independent confirmation that what FP8 loses above depth 3 is the row-count dependence rather than anything about speculative decoding.
speed: Depth 4 measures 177.69/177.45 against depth 3's 177.41/177.17 - a 0.16% difference, inside this lane's own noise, so the two are tied rather than depth 4 being an improvement. Depth 5 falls to 167.12/167.00 and depth 6 to 160.74/160.48. The hoped-for effect, that a cheaper target would make deeper drafts pay, does not appear: the 4B curve is flat to depth 4 and then falls, where the 9B fell immediately. Depth 3 stays the operating point on both models, now on each route's own evidence.
reading: Worth stating plainly because it is a negative for the optimization and a positive for the mechanism: no speed was found, and the identity prediction held on a second model.
